reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism of Platt scaling involves transforming raw classifier outputs into well-calibrated probabilities using an affine transformation within a logistic function. The IRLS method optimizes this by treating it as a weighted least squares problem with a Gaussian prior on the transformation parameters A and B. This dual formulation allows for iterative refinement where each step adjusts the parameters based on the gradient and Hessian of the negative log-likelihood plus the prior penalty. The resulting system is a fixed-point iteration that converges to a calibrated distribution. The parameters A and B have clear interpretations: A controls the spread of probabilities (compression when A<1, sharpening when A>1), while B shifts the entire distribution globally. These interpretations provide actionable insights for model calibration but also introduce potential failure modes such as overfitting due to improper prior specification or numerical instability during inversion of the Hessian matrix.
